goal: Help a home cook capture first, browse every local photo immediately, understand organization quietly, manually assign or correct any photo, manage dishes safely from Menu, build trustworthy cooking-event history, improve a dish cover safely, and plan one or more dishes for any selected day.

requirements.description: Plan and Menu keep the stable floating Plan–capture–Menu shell; Dishes remains the default Menu surface and a compact Photos button opens the dedicated gallery, with no permanent Capture, Inbox, Review, or Photos tab and no competing empty-state capture button.

Plan uses a horizontally pageable selected-day card where one date can contain multiple dishes, one clear add action targets that date, and an empty non-today date has the same add path without suggestion or review support cards.

The fixed calendar shows seven days per horizontal page, visually distinguishes today from the selected date, uses a clickable month/year caret to open date selection, provides one Today jump instead of week arrows, and demonstrates reaching a date outside the current week.

A planned dish row visibly opens details, its secondary action exposes Move to another day and Remove from plan, and removal remains reversible through a compact temporary Undo toast fixed above—not covering—the bottom navigation.

Take Photo and Import Photos capture without a destination decision; the local save closes Capture and places the real photo immediately in Photos with a quiet Organizing overlay while automatic existing-dish and new-dish outcomes remain reversible.

A newly saved photo remains fully viewable and manually organizable while background work is represented by a reduced-motion-safe animated Photos entry and one quiet Organizing overlay; either path opens usable photos rather than a technical job-status screen, and leaving detail does not cancel work.

Tapping any gallery tile opens an image-dominant photo detail state: unorganized photos expose Add to dish and Create new dish, organizing photos stay usable with Organize now, review photos present a clear local confirmation decision, and organized photos expose their dish plus View dish and Change dish paths.

A manual assignment applies locally first, moves the photo from Unorganized to Organized, identifies the chosen dish, offers atomic Undo, and is documented as authoritative over late AI proposals and safe across offline restart or retry.
Offline capture remains locally queued with a clear later-organizing state, while denied camera permission preserves Import Photos and Add Idea alternatives and explains the Settings recovery path.

Capture offers Take Photo, Import Photos, and Add Idea before any destination decision; Add Idea captures only a dish idea and optional memory note, with no planning controls, and has canonical valid and retained-content validation states.

AI uncertainty appears contextually as a restrained Review overlay and Unorganized filter count; opening that photo supports confirming the suggested dish, choosing another dish, or creating a new one, while alternate-dish search demonstrates clear query recovery.

Photos is a first-class image-dominant gallery inside Menu with All 18, Unorganized 5, and Organized 13 filters derived from local dish assignment; one subtle overlay per tile prioritizes Review, Couldn't organize, Organizing, Unorganized, then the assigned dish name without exposing upload or outbox vocabulary.

An unorganized photo exposes one primary Add to dish action, supports search and suggested existing dishes, creates one source in the captured-date cooking occasion, changes the reconciled counts from 5/13 to 4/14, and marks the association as durable user intent with Undo.

Delete remains subordinate in an overflow until a single destructive confirmation, clearly scopes removal to MyMenu while preserving the phone-library original and dish, returns to Unorganized with counts changed from 18/5/13 to 17/4/13, and offers a short Undo path before permanent removal.

Dish Detail presents Improve Cover as a persistent compact chip on the cover image; the flow explains that sources inform a new cover without changing originals, supports source selection and optional freeform visual direction, shows generation, compares current and proposed covers, and requires Use this cover or Keep current.
Offline and online-generation failure states both preserve the current cover and local dish knowledge, distinguish their causes, and provide non-destructive retry or exit paths.

Cook Again explains whether the user is cooking now or planning for later; the primary leftmost Journal combines photo occasions and standalone notes into one newest-first bulletin board where photos are visually primary, with icon-only add-photo and add-note actions. Journal and Recipe are adjacent horizontal pages, and their white selector slides continuously with tab taps or page swipes.

The single filterable Menu grid and first Dish Detail viewport read as a living cooking memory: new dishes have a styled top-left white New label that briefly wobbles as the card appears, every card keeps an always-visible top-right heart that changes from white to red when favorited, and Dish Detail opens on the photo-forward Journal.

Dishes labels the normal collection as 24 and the two-dish deletion result as 22 beside the All dishes heading, keeps an icon-only filter trigger fixed left of compact All, Favorites, and Recently added controls, uses icon-only newest/oldest sorting, and preserves the compact Photos entry in its search-empty state.

The shortened Dishes search leaves a stable trailing Photos button: neutral means no background work or unorganized photos, a stationary orange count means manual organization is available, and a subtle orbit plus sparkle means AI organization is active. The animation respects reduced motion, never shows a job count, and tapping opens the dedicated Photos gallery—on Unorganized when attention is needed—with a clear back path to Dishes.

The Photos collection covers empty, typical, dense/long-scroll, missing-thumbnail, background-processing, review, organization failure, unorganized, and organized states while keeping image tiles dominant, date groups stable, selection discoverable, and fixed navigation clear on every configured phone.

Long-pressing a finished dish gives haptic feedback, selects it, and replaces Dishes collection chrome with a close–count–Select all header; assistive technologies expose a semantic Select dish action without requiring the gesture. Multi-select works across current filtered results without opening dishes, allows ideas and dishes with no history, keeps destructive emphasis subordinate until one confirmation names the selected dishes and scopes dependent MyMenu removal while preserving phone-library originals, then applies locally, updates 24 to 22, and offers one atomic Undo.

Every normal Menu state uses compact fixed chrome: Dishes pairs shortened search with the trailing Photos status button and quick filters, while Photos uses a back action, title/count, organization filters, and Select. Chrome gains a shadow only after scrolling, and selection replaces collection controls in place.

Empty Dishes retains the neutral Photos entry and empty Photos retains a clear back path; both rely on the persistent global capture button as the only dominant action and use capture-first language rather than manual filing language.

The photo family extends the shared warm-minimal system while reducing card chrome: cream collection canvas, edge-dominant imagery, quiet translucent status labels, charcoal controls, orange reserved for the primary contextual action, and progressive destructive emphasis.

The shortened Dishes search and Photos status button, dedicated Photos title/back row, three-column gallery, filter counts, long dish overlay, missing-thumbnail tile, detail actions, picker completion, confirmation, and Undo remain readable and reachable on iPhone SE, iPhone 14, and Pixel 7 without clipped or covered controls.
Every delivery screen retains the shared cream, orange, charcoal, soft-surface, high-radius, rounded-type, and ambient-shadow system with one dominant filled action per task region.

Seven-day calendars, multiple planned dishes, compact sticky and replacement selection headers, long names, grouped history, comparison states, bottom actions, and recovery copy remain readable and reachable on iPhone SE, iPhone 14, and Pixel 7 without clipped or covered controls.
